title: Top 10 Attractions in Surat Thani 2026 — From Cheow Lan Dam to Ban Don Old Town | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Top 10 attractions in Surat Thani 2026: Ratchaprapha Dam (Cheow Lan), Koh Lamphu Island, Khao Tha Phet viewpoint, San Chao Market, Ban Don Walking Street, and Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya — with entry fees, directions, and trip-planning tips.

ogTitle: Top 10 Attractions in Surat Thani 2026 — See It Like a Local
ogDesc: Cheow Lan Dam, Khao Tha Phet, the old riverside town on the Tapi, a floating market in a coconut grove, and a Srivijaya-era temple in Chaiya — the most talked-about attractions in Surat Thani with trip-planning tips.
eyebrow: See Surat Thani Like a Local · Updated 2026
intro: Surat Thani is far more than a ferry stop for Koh Samui and Koh Phangan. The province itself has a limestone-cliff lake, an old riverside town along the Tapi River, a floating market in a coconut grove, and an ancient temple from the Srivijaya era. We picked the 10 attractions that locals and travellers talk about most — some are full-day trips, others are quick detours along the way.
chips: 🛶 Boat trip among the Three Friends hills
🍜 San Chao Market, Southern Thai food
☕ Café in the heart of town

blocks.html:
If you had to describe Surat Thani quickly, you'd say the city runs in several modes at once. In the morning you can jog or cycle around Koh Lamphu, a park island in the middle of the Tapi River, breathing in cool river air. By mid-morning head up Khao Tha Phet to look out over the whole city and the river mouth opening into the Gulf of Thailand. In the evening walk San Chao Market for Southern street food, and if it's a Saturday, continue to the Ban Don Walking Street along the Tapi, where a live-cooking zone is the highlight. Anyone wanting full-on nature can drive up toward Ban Ta Khun and take a longtail boat to see the Three Friends limestone peaks — Khao Sam Kloe — rising from the emerald water of Ratchaprapha Reservoir, known to many as Thailand's Guilin.

This list includes verified standouts. Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya Ratchaworawihan in Chaiya District is a royal temple of the first class, home to one of Thailand's most complete Srivijaya-style chedis. It's the essential stop for anyone on a temple circuit in Surat Thani. The city pillar shrine on the Tapi riverbank is the go-to blessing spot that locals visit regularly. For coffee lovers, Echo Coffee Roastery is an in-town roaster open every day, serving freshly roasted espresso in a clean, low-key space. Plan carefully and a single trip can cover nature, heritage, food, and a temple — all in one province.

blocks.name: Ratchaprapha Dam (Cheow Lan Dam) — Khao Sam Kloe Viewpoint
blocks.area: Ban Ta Khun District, Surat Thani
blocks.signature: Limestone peaks rising from emerald water, longtail boat tour to Khao Sam Kloe, floating raft house overnight on the lake
blocks.priceRange: ~40 THB national park entry + ~1,500–2,000 THB chartered boat
blocks.descHtml:
Ratchaprapha Dam — most people call it Cheow Lan Dam — is the reservoir above the dam in the middle of Khao Sok National Park, where limestone peaks jut through emerald water in rows that have earned the nickname "Thailand's Guilin." The star of the place is Khao Sam Kloe, three limestone hills standing prominently mid-lake and the most photographed landmark in the park. It works perfectly for couples, families, or groups of friends who want to spend a night on a floating raft house in the middle of a lake.

The highlight you cannot skip is chartering a longtail boat out to Khao Sam Kloe. The boat threads through gaps in the cliffs the whole way, giving you non-stop photo opportunities, and the round trip takes about two hours. If you have time, stay overnight on a raft — most reviews agree that the early morning mist drifting over the water is the most spectacular part. Wake up, jump into clear water, or paddle a kayak right off the front deck. Countless visitors say the scenery keeps wowing them no matter which direction they look — completely worth the journey.

On cost: national park entry is around 40 THB for Thais, plus a small local fee. A chartered longtail boat runs about 1,500–2,000 THB per vessel (2–3 passengers). Package stays that include the boat, meals, and activities start around 3,000–4,000 THB per person depending on the raft and number of nights. The site is in Ban Ta Khun District, roughly 1.5–2 hours by car from Surat Thani city. The boat pier and service area operate approximately 09:00–17:00 daily.

This place tops the list because the scenery is genuinely stunning and it works as a day trip or an overnight raft stay. Key things to know: Khao Sam Kloe is accessible only by boat. Book your raft and boat in advance, especially during long weekends when it fills up fast. Bring cash, sunscreen, and clothes that can get wet.
mustOrder: Boat tour among the Three Friends peaks on emerald water
Overnight raft stay, morning mist over the lake
Kayak or swim in clear water off the raft deck
Photos from Thailand's Guilin angles
blocks.bestFor: Couples, families, or friend groups who want a raft-house night and a boat tour

blocks.name: Koh Lamphu Public Park
blocks.area: Bang Bai Mai / Bang Kung Sub-district, Mueang Surat Thani District (island in the Tapi River)
blocks.signature: Green lung in the Tapi River — running and cycling track around the island, outdoor fitness zone, sunset views on the riverbank
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a place to walk and breathe fresh air in Surat Thani without driving out of town, Koh Lamphu is the first name locals think of. It's a public park on an island in the Tapi River, about 66 rai (26 acres), reached by crossing a footbridge from the city pillar shrine side. Cars can't enter, making it a quiet, shady green lung full of coconut palms and large trees. Great for morning exercise, families with kids, or anyone who wants to sit and watch the river flow by.

The main draw is the running and cycling track around the island — about 1.5 kilometres, with clearly separated lanes for each. Many reviews praise the clean surface and well-maintained outdoor fitness equipment. There's also a football pitch, basketball courts, a takraw court, and a TK Park learning zone for kids. The other thing visitors consistently mention is the Tapi River sunset in the late afternoon: golden light reflecting off longtail boats passing by. Some visitors spot squirrels in the trees and various birds too.

Cost is very easy — entry is free for everyone. There's a car park on the mainland side before the bridge, two toilet blocks, and bicycle rental at around 50 THB per hour if you didn't bring your own. The park opens from around 04:00 in the early morning until 22:00. Peak crowd time is evening, when the air cools and the whole neighbourhood comes out for a run.

A few things to know: midday sun is quite intense and it gets hot. Best times are early morning around 05:30–07:30 or evening 16:30–18:30. Mosquitoes pick up after dark, so bring repellent. A hat and sunscreen are useful. The park lights start going off around 21:00. It's popular because it's a rare large green space right in the city centre — easy to reach, free, and with genuinely beautiful river views.
mustOrder: Running/cycling track around the island (~1.5 km)
Outdoor fitness zone
Tapi River sunset view
TK Park learning zone
blocks.bestFor: Morning or evening exercise, and watching the Tapi River sunset
blocks.zone: City centre (island in the Tapi River)

blocks.name: San Chao Market (Ti Lek Lane Walking Street)
blocks.signature: Evening walking street open daily — Southern Thai food, rare traditional snacks, famous long-standing stalls
blocks.descHtml:
San Chao Market — locals call it the Ti Lek Lane Market — is the liveliest street-food walking street in the city centre. It's been here for over fifty years, entered through a red Chinese gate bearing the market's name, because the alley runs between a Chinese shrine and Wat Sai. Step inside and you find a long lane lined with over a hundred carts and food stalls on both sides. It's ideal for anyone who wants to eat and wander without planning much — fine on your own, as a couple, or in a group.

The standout that many recommend is the grilled fish cake on skewers, tossed in curry paste with kaffir lime leaves and holy basil — five sticks for twenty baht, something you won't easily find elsewhere. Pair it with traditional khanom buang, sweet or savoury, at thirty baht each. Another famous stall that has been operating for over twenty years is the charcoal-grilled pad thai, packed with smoky wok fragrance and sharp flavour. Beyond that you'll find grilled squid, other seafood, kanom jin with Southern curry sauce, fruit, desserts, and cold drinks — everything sweet and savoury under one roof.

The atmosphere is a genuinely old-style evening market: weathered shophouses all around, people jostling to queue. Busiest from 17:00 to 19:00. Open every day around 15:30–22:00. No entry fee — you pay only for what you eat. Two people can eat well for under 100 THB. The market is in the city centre near the Tapi River, a short walk from the illuminated bridge that photographs beautifully at night.

A few things to know: parking is tight because of crowds — park at the nearby temple or shrine for 10 THB. Most vendors speak limited English but pointing works fine. Ask prices before ordering at stalls with seating, especially grills. This market is popular because it's a genuine local market, offering authentic atmosphere and local flavours at very easy prices.
mustOrder: Grilled fish cake on skewers — a few baht each
Traditional khanom buang (savoury/sweet)
Charcoal-wok pad thai, old recipe
Grilled squid and seafood on the grill
blocks.bestFor: Dinner for street-food lovers, local flavours at light prices

blocks.name: Central Surat Thani
blocks.area: Wat Pradu Sub-district, Mueang Surat Thani District
blocks.signature: Large resort-style shopping centre — Robinson, SF Cinema, Fun Planet indoor amusement park, Chill-Lay night market out front
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a cool, easy evening out in Surat Thani with everything in one place, Central Surat Thani is where locals and tourists head most. It's a large resort-style open mall that opened in 2012 as the first Central in the Upper South. Inside you'll find Robinson as the anchor store, alongside Tops Market, B2S, PowerBuy, Supersports, Uniqlo, and Charles & Keith — all in one building. A good fit for families, couples hunting for a café spot, or travellers who just want somewhere air-conditioned to decompress.

Highlights to catch: the seven-screen SF Cinema for film fans, the Fun Planet indoor amusement park that kids love, and the Pet Planet zone. The food zone and various restaurants cover a wide range of options. In the evenings a night market called Chill-Lay Market opens out front — many reviews say it's fun to walk through, with Southern street food and a relaxed crowd.

No worries on budget: there's no entry fee, and parking is ample front and back with no stress. Come just to browse in the AC or commit to a proper shopping day — either way works. Costs depend on what you eat and watch. Starting from a few hundred baht, you'll be set for the whole day. The mall is open every day 10:00–21:00, located in Wat Pradu Sub-district on the bypass road connecting the city centre to the airport.

It's popular because it's the city's hub for nearly everything. Google ratings sit at 4.6 from several thousand reviews, with people praising the cleanliness, air conditioning, free Wi-Fi, and helpful staff. One tip: weekends and holidays fill up fast, especially near the main entrances. Come a little earlier if you want easier parking, and if you want the night market out front, come in the early evening.
mustOrder: SF Cinema — seven screens
Fun Planet indoor amusement park
Chill-Lay night market out front
Robinson + Tops Market
blocks.bestFor: Family outings or all-day browsing in the cool

blocks.name: Surat Thani City Pillar Shrine
blocks.signature: Ancient Thai-style city pillar shrine on the Tapi riverbank — a Ratchaphruek-wood pillar topped with four-faced Bodhisattva, the city's go-to blessing spot
blocks.descHtml:
The Surat Thani City Pillar Shrine is a white Srivijaya-style shrine right on the Tapi riverbank, directly opposite Si Tapi Bridge. A good first stop for anyone arriving in the city centre, whether a local or a traveller coming through the Ban Don pier. The heart of the place is the city pillar carved from Ratchaphruek wood, its top carved with four faces of the Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara looking out in all four directions — rare to see at a city pillar shrine anywhere else in Thailand. It was built to commemorate the 50th anniversary of King Rama IX's reign.

The thing most people come to do is buy a pre-assembled offering set available in two sizes — 50 THB or 100 THB — containing flowers, incense sticks, a candle, lamp oil, gold leaf, and coloured fabric to tie around the four replica pillars. Light the incense, press gold leaf onto the pillar base, and strike the gong inside the building. Signs explain the steps and the prayer clearly, so nothing to worry about. Several real reviews note that the staff are friendly and always ready to guide visitors. The whole circuit takes only a short while and fits easily into a single trip.

The atmosphere is clean, peaceful, and has elephant statues and flowers arranged at the entrance. Reviews consistently say midday sun is fierce, but evenings are comfortable. At night the building is lit up in changing colours, making it another favourite photo spot — some foreign reviewers call it among the most beautiful city shrines they've seen in Thailand. Google rating is 4.7 from over 1,300 reviews, which means people are very satisfied.

Free entry, with a donation box if you want to make an offering. The location is in the city centre near Talat Mai Road, easy to find, and accessible by private vehicle, songthaew, or taxi. Street parking is available around the shrine. Note: shoes off when entering the shrine building, and dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees. Open around 08:00–19:00. If you want both a blessing and a beautiful lit-up photo, late afternoon into early evening is the sweet spot.
mustOrder: Ratchaphruek-wood pillar topped with four-faced Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara
Tie coloured fabric, press gold leaf, strike the gong
Srivijaya-style building on the Tapi River lit up at night
View of Si Tapi Bridge across the river
blocks.bestFor: A blessing at the city shrine, photos in the evening when the lights come on
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Surat Thani City Pillar Shrine · Oatz · Wikimedia Commons · Public Domain

blocks.title: 🛏️ Book accommodation in Surat Thani
blocks.text: Pick your base to match your style of trip. Staying in Ban Don city centre puts you close to San Chao Market, the walking street, cafés, and the city pillar shrine — great for exploring the town and eating well. If you're focused on nature, try booking a raft house on Cheow Lan Lake in Ban Ta Khun for a night — wake up to a view of limestone peaks rising from the water. Book ahead during long weekends to secure good rooms and well-positioned rafts.

blocks.name: Bang Bai Mai Pracharath Floating Market (Klong Roi Sai)
blocks.area: Bang Bai Mai Sub-district, Mueang Surat Thani District, Surat Thani
blocks.cuisine: Southern home cooking / traditional Thai desserts
blocks.signature: Community floating market in a coconut-palm grove — boat ride through a nipa-palm tunnel, local snacks, traditional food
blocks.priceRange: Free entry · Boat ride 20 THB/person or charter 100 THB
blocks.descHtml:
If you want to see authentic Surat Thani canal life without driving far, the Bang Bai Mai Pracharath Floating Market is the answer. It's a community market in the middle of a coconut grove and nipa-palm stands, beside Wat Bang Bai Mai, only about ten minutes from the city. The highlight is that local residents from the sub-district run over a hundred food stalls themselves, creating a calm, shady, relaxed atmosphere that's perfect for anyone who has had enough of busy urban markets and wants something slower and more genuine. Open Sundays only — check your day carefully before planning.

The most talked-about activity is the boat ride through the nipa-palm tunnel — a natural archway of nipa palms bending together overhead. The wooden rowing boat threads through Klong Roi Sai, past nipa forest, swamp apple trees, and riverside houses, taking about half an hour. Boat fare is 20 THB per person, or charter a boat for about 100 THB (seats about 5). Many reviews say the scenery exceeded expectations and photographs beautifully. For food, try traditional snacks like khanom chang, palm sugar, palm juice, Surat-style pad thai, and fresh seafood at very gentle prices — most dishes are just a few tens of baht.

Budget-wise it's extremely easy: free entry, main costs are the boat ride and the food you want to try. A whole morning here costs only a few hundred baht and you'll leave full and with souvenirs. The market is in Bang Bai Mai Sub-district, Mueang Surat Thani, open every Sunday from around 09:00–16:00. There's parking, toilets, and a riverside sala for resting. Come early for the best selection, thinner crowds, and cooler air.

This market is popular because it combines three things hard to find together: the natural canal scenery, affordable traditional food, and genuinely welcoming community members who smile and serve you themselves. Note: open Sundays only. The nipa-palm tunnel looks its best at high tide — ask the boat crew about the tide window before you board.
mustOrder: Boat ride through the nipa-palm tunnel, Klong Roi Sai
Khanom chang and traditional ancient desserts
Palm sugar, palm juice
Surat-style pad thai
blocks.bestFor: Sunday breakfast outing, nature lovers and a relaxed boat ride

blocks.name: Khao Tha Phet (Surat Thani City Viewpoint)
blocks.signature: Panoramic viewpoint over Surat Thani, the Tapi River, and the Gulf of Thailand — plus an old hilltop temple and a large reclining Buddha
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Tha Phet is a low hill on the outskirts of Surat Thani, only about 6 kilometres south of the city by car. It is home to Phra That Si Surat, a slender spire-shaped chedi about 30 metres tall on the summit — a sacred landmark that residents of Ban Don have revered since the 1950s. The site suits anyone wanting a combination of temple visit, city views, and a breath of forest air without venturing far. Families, couples, or solo visitors all manage it comfortably, and the road up the hill is gentle enough for a standard car.

The highlight people talk about most is the viewpoint looking down over Surat Thani with the Tapi River winding through it, and on clear days you can see it opening into the Gulf of Thailand. Real reviews consistently say it is the only hilltop near the city that gives a proper full panorama — some visitors say they could spot Koh Prab island. The misty early morning, when light haze clings to the forest and hills, feels especially cool and peaceful. The must-dos are paying respect to the phra that on the summit, walking through the shady trees of the wildlife sanctuary, and shooting city views from the observation point.

No entry fee for either the phra that area or the viewpoint. The hill sits within the 2,900-rai (about 1,160-acre) Khao Tha Phet Wildlife Sanctuary, thick with dry evergreen forest and large trees. You may encounter monkeys and forest birds. The nature education centre inside opens Monday–Friday around 09:00–16:00, closed Saturday–Sunday, but the phra that and the observation deck above are open every day. Most people come in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat and catch the best light.

This is the only place near the city that delivers a panoramic view, green forest, and a sacred site all at once, plus an annual robe-wrapping ceremony that draws a lively local crowd. Things to note: the road up is narrow and winds a bit — drive slowly and watch for oncoming vehicles. Bring water and sunscreen, as shops on the hill are limited. Choose a clear-sky day for the sharpest views.
mustOrder: Viewpoint over Surat Thani, the Tapi River, and the Gulf
Pay respects at Phra That Si Surat on the summit
Walk through the wildlife sanctuary forest
Morning mist over the hills
blocks.bestFor: City viewpoint + morning or evening temple visit
blocks.hours: Observation deck/phra that open daily (nature centre Mon–Fri 09:00–16:00)

blocks.name: Ang Thong Marine National Park
blocks.signature: 42 limestone islands in the Gulf of Thailand — the Emerald Lake, a hidden emerald lagoon inside the main island
blocks.priceRange: 300 THB foreigners (150 THB children) / 40 THB Thais + tour boat from Samui or Phangan
blocks.descHtml:
Ang Thong Marine National Park is an archipelago of 42 limestone islands in the Gulf of Thailand, west of Koh Samui, ideal for anyone who wants to escape crowded beaches for full-on nature — photographers, kayakers, and families with children who want to play in clear water. The highlight that everyone seeks out is the Emerald Lake on Ko Mae Koh, a saltwater lagoon of emerald green enclosed on all sides by sheer limestone cliffs. You hike up steep stairs to the viewpoint above to see the full picture — and the effort is completely worth the reward.

Beyond the Emerald Lake there's a viewpoint on Ko Wua Talap where you climb up and look out over islands stretching to the horizon, kayaking activities along cliff faces and through sea caves, and snorkelling in clear shallow water. The overall feel is a raw natural island — transparent blue water, quiet white sand beaches. In the late morning tour boats may arrive in clusters, but once you walk into the individual spots you can always find a clear angle for photos.

The only way in is by tour boat, mostly day trips leaving from Koh Samui and Koh Phangan, with speedboats and larger vessels to choose from. Tour prices typically include transfers, meals, and snorkelling gear. National park fees: foreign adults 300 THB, children 150 THB; Thai adults 40 THB, children 20 THB. Open approximately 08:00–17:00. Note: during the monsoon, the park typically closes from around 1 November until mid-to-late December when seas are rough — check with your tour operator before booking.

People keep coming because they get to see the real Emerald Lake they've only ever seen on travel posters, plus kayaking, snorkelling, and a hilltop view in one trip. One important warning: the path up to the Emerald Lake and the viewpoint is fairly steep — wear shoes with good grip, bring drinking water and sunscreen, and allow for heat and possible crowds.
mustOrder: Emerald Lake on Ko Mae Koh
Ko Wua Talap viewpoint
Kayaking and snorkelling around the islands
blocks.bestFor: Day trip by boat — Emerald Lake, kayaking, snorkelling
blocks.hours: Seasonal ~08:00–17:00; closed during monsoon ~1 Nov–mid/late Dec
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Ang Thong marine lagoon · Vyacheslav Argenberg · Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 4.0

blocks.name: Echo Coffee Roastery
blocks.area: Mueang Surat Thani District, Surat Thani
blocks.cuisine: Specialty coffee roastery and café, light meals
blocks.signature: In-house coffee roastery — fresh-roasted beans, clean minimal interior, open daily
blocks.descHtml:
If you're stopping through Surat Thani and want coffee that takes itself seriously, Echo Coffee Roastery is the place. It's both a roastery and a café in one — roasting its own beans on-site with a team holding Q Grader and SCA certifications. The actual differentiator is the freshly roasted coffee: they source beans from multiple origins and roast them in-house to pull out the character of each one. Great for coffee people who want clear, defined flavours, and for anyone who likes a clean, minimal space to sit and shoot a photo. The shop has a dark tonal interior that feels sharp and simple, with both an indoor zone and a garden section outside.

Drinks people mention most often are the Corn Dirty — an espresso with sweet corn milk — and Burn Out, which blends espresso, lime, paprika, and vanilla cream in a way that sounds odd but lands well. For something brighter and fresh, Wake Up is a raw-sugar espresso with lime and salt, and Very Berry mixes espresso with berry juice. Importantly, it's not just coffee: the kitchen also does khao soi, truffle spaghetti, and homemade desserts, making it a proper one-stop for a meal. The owner has won at the Santoker Thailand competition, which is a decent quality marker.

Prices are approachable: signature drinks around 95 THB, main dishes approximately 175–195 THB, average spend per person from under a hundred to around 250 THB. If you want beans to take home, they range from 250 THB (250 g, dark roast) to 350 THB (200 g, light roast). The shop is in the Makham Tia area of Surat Thani city, on Chon Kaset Road — easy to reach from the airport and the bus terminal, with ample parking. Open every day 07:30–20:00.

What people like is the relaxed atmosphere, staff who talk about coffee with genuine enthusiasm, and the second floor co-working zone with good natural light. The Google review score sits at 4.8 from several hundred reviews — strong feedback for a relatively new shop. One tip: it gets busy on weekends, and the kitchen stops taking orders before closing time — give yourself enough time if you want to eat.
mustOrder: Corn Dirty — espresso with corn milk
Burn Out — espresso with lime and paprika
Khao soi
Fresh-roasted beans to take home
blocks.bestFor: Café hoppers and fresh-roasted coffee lovers

blocks.name: Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya Ratchaworawihan
blocks.signature: Thailand's most complete Srivijaya-style chedi — the province's essential temple for merit-making and heritage
blocks.descHtml:
If you want to combine a temple visit with genuine historical discovery in Surat Thani, Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya Ratchaworawihan is the place not to miss. This is a royal temple of the first class in Chaiya District, about 54 kilometres from the city. The centrepiece is the Phra Borommathat chedi in Srivijaya style — a square-cornered base rising about 24 metres — that many regard as the most complete Srivijaya-era chedi in Thailand. It has stood for over a thousand years. Suitable for those on a temple circuit, history enthusiasts, and anyone who wants calm, beautiful photos away from crowds.

The must-do is walking in devotion around the chedi, which enshrines the Buddha's relics, and then walking the cloister gallery where nearly two hundred ancient Buddha images are arranged in rows, including sandstone images from the Ayutthaya period. If you're genuinely interested in antiquities, continue to the Chaiya National Museum within the same grounds — it displays the Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara and Srivijaya-period artefacts up close. Real reviews from multiple visitors say the place feels shady, clean, and generously car-parked, with a genuinely peaceful feeling.

Very easy on the wallet: entering the temple and paying respects to the chedi is free. The national museum charges separately — Thais 20 THB, foreigners 120 THB. Open Wednesday–Sunday. The temple itself opens daily approximately 07:30–17:00. Driving yourself is the most convenient option; arriving by train to Chaiya station and taking a short connection works too.

This temple is popular because it is the true ancestral temple of Surat Thani — its chedi image is even used as the provincial emblem. Google score is 4.7 from several thousand reviews. Things to note: this is a sacred site — dress modestly, and come in the morning when the sun is cooler. If you're in Chaiya, visit this temple first, then continue to Suan Mokkh garden monastery or look for Chaiya salted eggs to take home.
mustOrder: Pay respects to the 24-metre Srivijaya chedi
Walk the cloister with ancient Buddha images
Visit Chaiya National Museum
Photograph the chedi — the provincial emblem
blocks.bestFor: Temple and history enthusiasts — come in the morning on a Chaiya day trip

blocks.title: Book tours and tickets in Surat Thani
blocks.text: If you want to cover multiple attractions in a day without driving yourself or negotiating boat prices, booking a tour through Klook or GetYourGuide is the way to go. Cheow Lan Dam day trips and overnight raft packages typically include transfers, the boat, and a guide — so you can enjoy the Three Friends peaks without sorting logistics at the pier yourself. Good for anyone with limited time who wants everything ready to go.

blocks.title: What to know before visiting Surat Thani

items.title: Renting a car beats public transport for out-of-town spots
items.text: Grab works fine in the city, but Cheow Lan Dam in Ban Ta Khun and Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya in Chaiya are far away with limited public transport. Renting a car or hiring a driver is the most flexible option.

items.title: Markets and street food run on cash
items.text: San Chao Market, Ban Don Walking Street, and Bang Bai Mai Floating Market mostly accept cash or Thai QR scans. Keep some small bills handy. Cafés and the mall in the city accept cards.

items.title: Get to Cheow Lan Dam early
items.text: Book a morning boat tour to see Khao Sam Kloe — calmer water, better light, and no queue. Ban Don Walking Street runs Saturday evenings only — check the day before planning.

items.title: Dress modestly at temples
items.text: Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya and the city pillar shrine are sacred places — cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes at designated points, and keep voices low inside the temple grounds.

items.title: English menus exist in some places but not everywhere
items.text: Malls and cafés like Echo Coffee Roastery usually have English menus, but market stalls may only have Thai. A translation app that reads images works well; Surat Thani locals are friendly and always willing to help.

items.title: Booking tours ahead cuts hassle
items.text: Popular Cheow Lan Dam raft stays fill up fast during long weekends. Booking through Klook or GetYourGuide gives you a fixed price and means no last-minute scrambling at the pier.

blocks.title: How to plan a strong 2-day Surat Thani trip
blocks.html:
With two days, split into one city day and one nature day. Day one: stay in the city, starting in the morning at Koh Lamphu Public Park or Khao Tha Phet before the sun gets fierce. Midday, swing by Echo Coffee Roastery — open every day, drinks around 95–195 THB. Then pay respects at the city pillar shrine on the Tapi. End the evening at San Chao Market, or Ban Don Walking Street if it falls on a Saturday.

Day two: go all-in on nature. Drive up to Ban Ta Khun for Ratchaprapha Dam (Cheow Lan Dam) — arrive at the pier in the morning to book a chartered boat for Khao Sam Kloe. Park entry is around 40 THB and a chartered boat runs roughly 1,500–2,000 THB per vessel. If you have more time, add Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya in Chaiya District — it's in a different direction, so keep it as a separate day for a more relaxed pace.

blocks.text: To cover both the city and Cheow Lan Dam properly, picking a well-placed base in Surat Thani makes moving between spots much easier. A city-centre stay puts you close to the market and cafés; for a nature focus, try booking a raft house on Cheow Lan Lake for a night.

faq.q: Which Surat Thani attraction should I not miss?
faq.a: For a first visit, Ratchaprapha Dam (Cheow Lan Dam) in Ban Ta Khun District is the one — take a longtail boat to see Khao Sam Kloe, limestone peaks rising from emerald water, which is the defining image of the province. Pair it with Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya Ratchaworawihan in Chaiya District, one of Thailand's most complete Srivijaya-era chedis.

faq.q: What are the highlights of Surat Thani?
faq.a: It covers every type of traveller. Nature: Cheow Lan Dam and the Khao Tha Phet viewpoint overlooking the city and the Tapi River mouth. Old town and food: San Chao Market and Ban Don Walking Street along the Tapi. Community life: Bang Bai Mai Pracharath Floating Market in Klong Roi Sai. Temple visits: the city pillar shrine and Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya. And for coffee: Echo Coffee Roastery.

faq.q: How much does entry cost at Surat Thani attractions?
faq.a: Most are free: Koh Lamphu, Khao Tha Phet, the city pillar shrine, San Chao Market, and Ban Don Walking Street. Ratchaprapha Dam charges around 40 THB park entry plus about 1,500–2,000 THB for a chartered boat. Bang Bai Mai Floating Market is free to enter, boat rides around 20 THB per person. Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya is free; the museum charges around 20 THB.

faq.q: Is getting around and parking in Surat Thani convenient?
faq.a: City spots like Koh Lamphu, the city pillar shrine, San Chao Market, and Central all have parking and are Grab-accessible. Out-of-town spots like Cheow Lan Dam in Ban Ta Khun and Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya in Chaiya are far from the city — renting a car or hiring a private driver is the most practical. Evenings in the walking street area get crowded; park just outside and walk in.

faq.q: What are the opening hours at Surat Thani attractions?
faq.a: San Chao Market opens every evening. Ban Don Walking Street is Saturday evenings only. Echo Coffee Roastery opens daily around 07:30–20:00. Cheow Lan Dam: arrive at the pier in the morning to book a boat and catch the best light. Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya opens daily for worship — come in the morning to early afternoon to visit the museum too.
